newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says 98 deficit cuts to stay at 25 trln lire.
newsitem.headline: Italy says 98 deficit cuts to stay at 25 trln lire.

text.p: Treasury and Budget Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Sunday that Italy's 1998 deficit reduction measures will total 25 trillion lire, as established in the government's three-year economic plan.

"The government has established and the Parliament has approved deficit-cutting measures of 25 trillion lire. That is how it is and that is how it will remain," Ciampi said in an interview with RAI state radio GR1.

Italian newspapers reported this weekend that the Italian Treasury was seeking a further three trillion lire of cuts in next year's financial budget to counter an extra three trillion lire of spending on education, extra pensions and other items.

In late May, Prime Minister Romano Prodi unveiled Italy's three-year economic plan which outlined that the 1998 budget would slice 25 trillion lire off the state deficit by combining 15 trillion lire of spending cuts with 10 trillion lire of revenue-raising measures.
